She stated that the neighbors approached her expressing their fear about the proximity of
the trees to their home after the storms. The neighbor asked if they could get three quotes
to trim the trees to make them hurricane-proof. She stated that she did meet with all three
companies and felt that Blaze Tree Service was very knowledgeable. She admitted that she
knew very little about trees, only that she didn’t want one causing injury. She felt the
responsible thing to do was to cut back the trees and took the advice of Blaze Tree Service
because initially she wanted the Magnolia tree removed. She said the permit was denied,
but Blaze told her they would trim and shape  it. She wanted the two Live Oaks to be
hurricane-proof; that it was the objective of hiring the service.

She said it was quite expensive for them at the time, $1,700.00, after the permit was denied
for the Magnolia tree. The neighbors offered to help with the cost. She stated that the trees
have come back and are green. She stated she was only trying to do the right thing.

Ms. Blaney asked Ms. Young if Blaze provided her with any documents from an arborist or
landscape architect. Ms. Young replied no. She stated that she received three notices from
the city, but she felt there was an error. The first notice was only sent to her and her
husband.  She called and spoke with J.J. Torres-Rodriguez, the city Arborist, on many
occasions, and he told her not to worry. The second notice was to Blaze Tree Service,
noting her name wasn’t on it. The third came about two weeks ago, addressed to Blaze
Tree Service and her and her husband.
